newsitem.title: USA: American Skiing Co. buys two western ski resorts.
newsitem.headline: American Skiing Co. buys two western ski resorts.

text.p: The "Beast of the East" is moving west. Maine-based American Skiing Co. agreed Friday to buy two western ski resorts for $288 million in a deal that would make it the biggest ski resort operator in the United States.

American Skiing agreed to buy Steamboat Ski Resort in Steamboat Springs, Colo., and Heavenly Ski Resort in Lake Tahoe on the California-Nevada border from Kamori International Corp., a closely held company that also owns hotels in Japan and assets at a French ski resort.
"This is a big day for us," ASC Chairman Les Otten said. "These are resorts that are highly respected among skiers and snowboarders because both deliver an outstanding experience."

The deal, the latest in a wave of consolidation in the North American ski industry, will give ASC a major presence in the west and make it slightly larger than rivals Vail Resorts Inc. of Colorado and Vancouver-based Intrawest Corp.

"Those are big acquisitions," said analyst Kevin Eldridge at Salman Partners, a research firm in Vancouver, British Columbia. "Those two mountains give them a real step up in terms of critical mass. I would consider them (ASC) on par with Vail and Intrawest now."
During the previous ski season, the Steamboat and Heavenly resorts had an estimated 1.75 million skier days, an industry measure accounting for one skier skiing all or part of a day.
The two additional resorts combined with its nine other resorts give ASC a total of about 4.9 million skier days for the previous season, spokesman Skip King said.
Intrawest, which paid about $190 million in December to buy Copper Mountain in Colorado and Whistler Mountain in British Columbia, said at the time it expected to have about 4.6 million skier days.
Vail Resorts, which grew to four Colorado ski areas through a $300 million merger earlier this year, had 4.89 million skier days for the previous season, a spokeswoman said.
ASC had been active in the industry consolidation but until this year, all its resorts were based in the Northeast.

ASC dominated the eastern market with its Vermont resort Killington, marketed as the "Beast of the East", its flagship Sunday River resort in Maine and six other ski areas. But ASC wanted a world-class resort in the west to raise its profile, Eldridge said.
"They've been looking for a sizeable acquisition in the west," Eldridge said. "One of the big problems for American Skiing was they were very geographically focused on the East Coast."
Earlier this summer, ASC bought the tiny Wolf Mountain ski resort in Park City, Utah. ASC renamed the resort The Canyons and will invest $18 million in ski operations this year.
With the addition of the Steamboat and Heavenly resorts, more than half of ASC's skier visits will be from its western resorts, company spokesman King said.
The deal raised speculation that ASC might go public with a stock offering to raise funds and better compete with its rivals.
Otten said in an interview it was inappropriate to discuss financing for the deal at this time.
The transaction removes two of the premier names from a dwindling list of world-class ski resorts up for grabs.
